- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak for next 7–14 days.
- If sentiment turns negative after a peak, model fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is weak (0.00–0.33) and price is trending downward; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias for next 3–7 days.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending sideways, model often lags; forecast should be adjusted to match recent 3–5 day average, not 30d trend.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is below 70% of 30d mean, model is overconfident; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 10–20 days.
- If sentiment is positive but price is falling, model often misreads sentiment; reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until sentiment reverses.
